final_review: The development of zero-shot learning vision-language models has gained significant attention in recent years (Radford et al., 2021; Zhou et al., 2022). These models aim to learn transferable visual models from natural language supervision, enabling them to perform tasks without requiring large amounts of labeled data (Radford et al., 2021). The use of noisy text supervision has also been explored, with studies demonstrating its effectiveness in scaling up visual and vision-language representation learning (Jia et al., 2021). Furthermore, the availability of large-scale datasets, such as LAION-5B, has facilitated the training of next-generation image-text models (Schuhmann et al., 2022). The application of deep learning concepts, including CNN architectures, has been instrumental in the development of vision-language models (Alzubaidi et al., 2021). However, challenges such as reproducibility and scalability remain, with studies highlighting the need for reproducible scaling laws for contrastive language-image learning (Cherti et al., 2023). In addition, the use of large language models has been shown to encode clinical knowledge, with potential applications in medical imaging (Singhal et al., 2023). The use of data augmentation techniques, including text and image data augmentation, has also been explored, with studies highlighting their potential in improving model performance (Shorten et al., 2021; Shorten et al., 2019). However, contradictions exist in the literature, with some studies suggesting that the use of large language models may not always lead to improved performance (Wijegunarathna et al., 2023). Moreover, research gaps remain, including the need for further exploration of the applications of vision-language models in medical imaging (Coelho, 2023). In conclusion, the development of zero-shot learning vision-language models has made significant progress in recent years, with studies demonstrating the effectiveness of approaches such as natural language supervision and noisy text supervision (Radford et al., 2021; Jia et al., 2021). However, challenges and research gaps remain, highlighting the need for further research in this area. The use of large-scale datasets, such as Visual Genome, has also facilitated the development of vision-language models, with potential applications in a range of fields (Krishna et al., 2017).
